title: Why You Jolt When Someone Appears In Your Peripheral Vision
hook: Your brain thinks every shadow is a predator.

narration.text: That sudden jolt when someone enters your peripheral vision is an ancient alarm.
It is your brain's primal threat detection system firing instantly.
Even before conscious recognition, your brain prioritises potential danger.
This quick response kept our ancestors safe from hidden threats.
It means your subconscious is always on high alert for movement.
So next time, remember it is your survival instinct at work.
Did this surprise you? Like and subscribe for more insights into your mind, and share this with a jumpy friend.

description: Ever wondered why a sudden movement at the edge of your vision makes you jump? It is not just you; it is a fascinating survival mechanism from our ancestors. Your brain is wired to detect potential threats instantly.
topic: Why you often feel a jolt of alarm when someone unexpectedly appears in your peripheral vision. This is your ancient threat detection system.
